fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective posts on both sides to define the edge of the access point, particularly if vegetation narrows the opening.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the driveway to maintain a clear path wide enough for emergency vehicles.
• Keep the driveway clear of parked vehicles so emergency apparatus can reach the residence without delay.
• Trim dense vegetation between the main residence and the detached structure to keep a clear path between the two buildings for responders moving on foot.
• Cut back dense vegetation along the rear and sides of the property to allow responders to move around the buildings without obstruction.
• Mark any rear or side gate with a visible sign and keep it unlocked so responders can reach the back of the property without losing time.
• Post the property address visibly on the detached structure if it sits away from the street and could cause confusion during an emergency response.
• Keep the walkway clear of obstacles so responders can move quickly between the parking area and the main entry.
• Identify a flat, open staging area near the driveway, such as the vehicle parking area or open lawn, and keep it free of stored items so responders have room to work.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim branches from trees that hang directly over or touch the house roof and walls.
• Thin the tree cluster nearest to the structure to create open space between individual trees.
• Remove shrubs growing directly against the base of the structure.
• Clear low-hanging branches from trees along the driveway to keep the travel path open overhead.
• Thin shrubs and small vegetation along both sides of the driveway to maintain clear sight lines and passage.
• Remove or cut back vegetation crowding the rear of the property to open a path for access behind the structure.
• Separate shrub groupings near the structure so there are open gaps between them and the building.
• Trim the lower branches of scattered trees near the structure up from the ground to reduce the connection between ground-level plants and tree canopies.
• Keep the open green space areas mowed or cut short to limit the spread of fire across those areas toward the structure.
